title: Outage: the shop returns 503 while every pod is Running

lines.text: 09:15 alert: shop.example.com returns 503 for every request; the 10:00 flash sale email has already gone out
08:58 Git: merged 'tidy labels' (shop-web manifests); Argo CD synced shop-web
Argo CD: shop-web OutOfSync, self-heal applied Git's Service again; shop.example.com returns 503
deployment.apps "shop-web" deleted: every shop-web pod is terminating
10:00 the flash sale started with the shop down; customers are getting 503

objective: Troubleshooting: where to look when a node, a Service or the control plane misbehaves, and the role of metrics-server and probes in detecting failure
secondaryObjectives: Debugging a delivery: rolling back safely and recognizing configuration drift between Git and the cluster
Core concepts: namespaces, labels, selectors and annotations, and how Services, Deployments and policies select the Pods they act on

Relevant text: with 'selfHeal: true' Argo CD syncs 'when the live cluster's state deviates from the state defined in Git'; 'The automatic sync interval is determined by the timeout.reconciliation value in the argocd-cm ConfigMap, which defaults to 120s with added jitter of 60s for a maximum period of 3 minutes.' brief.situation: You are on call for a fictional online shop. At 09:15 shop.example.com started returning 503 for every request. A flash sale starts at 10:00 and the email has already gone out. At 08:58 someone merged a 'tidy labels' change to the shop-web manifests, and Argo CD synced it.
handover: shop-web is a Deployment of 3 pods behind a ClusterIP Service and an Ingress. Argo CD keeps the cluster in sync with Git, with self-heal on: a change made only in the cluster is put back to what Git says.
Node w2 runs a nightly report job that keeps its CPU busy every morning.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes your time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The sale keeps coming on the same clock, and Argo CD keeps reconciling on it.
The map shows the Ingress, Service, Deployment, Argo CD and the nodes, each with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the shop restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The sale starts at 10:00, 45 minutes after the first alert.

source.cite: Argo CD documentation, Automated Sync Policy
source.note: FLAG: the documentation gives the reconciliation interval (120 s plus up to 60 s jitter, at most 3 minutes) but no number for how soon self-heal reverts a live edit; 3 minutes is the author's teaching value.

options.label: git revert the 'tidy labels' commit, push, and sync in Argo CD
kubectl set selector on the live Service: app=shop-web
kubectl label the running pods app=shopweb to match the Service

then.output:
$ git revert a7d93f1 && git push
$ argocd app sync shop-web
Service shop/shop-web configured (selector app=shop-web)

then.log: Git has the right selector again and Argo CD synced it.

then.output:
$ kubectl set selector svc shop-web app=shop-web
service/shop-web selector updated

then.log: The live Service now selects the pods; Git still has app=shopweb.

then.output:
$ kubectl label pods -l app=shop-web app=shopweb --overwrite
pod/shop-web-7c9d8f6b5-4kq2x labeled (and 2 more)

then.log: The three relabeled pods now match the Service, but no longer the ReplicaSet's selector: it starts three new app=shop-web pods, and the relabeled ones run unmanaged until someone deletes them.

then.output:
$ kubectl delete deployment shop-web
deployment.apps "shop-web" deleted

then.log: Every shop-web pod is terminating. Nothing serves the shop now, whatever the Service selects.

then.output:
$ kubectl rollout restart deployment shop-web
deployment.apps/shop-web restarted

then.log: New pods come up Ready with the same labels; the Service still selects nothing.

writeup.question: For the incident record: where you looked and what ruled things out, what the cause was and how you proved it, and why your fix will stay fixed.

parts.label: Where you looked
parts.criteria: Pods Running and Ready (probes passing) rule out the app; the busy node's kubectl top numbers are not the cause; the Service with no endpoints is the break between Ingress and pods.
parts.modelAnswer: All three pods were Running and Ready, so the readiness probes passed and the app was fine. kubectl top showed w2 busy, but that happens every morning and Ready pods were not getting traffic at all. kubectl describe svc showed Endpoints <none>.

parts.label: Cause and proof
parts.criteria: Compares the Service selector (app=shopweb) with the pod labels (app=shop-web) and traces the typo to the merged Git change.
parts.modelAnswer: The Service selected app=shopweb and the pods are labeled app=shop-web, so the EndpointSlice controller found nothing. argocd app diff and git log showed the typo came in with the 'tidy labels' commit.

parts.label: A fix that stays
parts.criteria: Fixes it in Git (revert) and syncs, explaining that a live patch or hand labels drift from Git and self-heal or the next rollout undoes them; verifies with a request.
parts.modelAnswer: I reverted the commit and synced, so Git and the cluster agree. A kubectl patch would have worked for three minutes until self-heal put Git's selector back; hand labels vanish with the next rollout. curl returned 200.

reasoningCriteria.label: Written triage, proof and lasting fix

expertPath.text: kubectl get pods: 3/3 Running and Ready, no restarts. The app and its probes are fine.
kubectl describe svc and the EndpointSlice: no endpoints; selector app=shopweb. --show-labels: the pods are app=shop-web.
argocd app diff and git log: the typo came from 'tidy labels'. git revert, push, sync.
curl returns 200. Record the cause; ask for a check in CI that every Service selects at least one pod template.

fixed.headline: Good: fixed in Git
fixed.body: Running, Ready pods and an empty endpoint list pointed at the selector; you found the typo, traced it to the merge and fixed it where Argo CD reads it.

fixedGaps.headline: Restored, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: The shop answers. The criteria show what it cost: time, a live-only change that drifts from Git, or restarts the evidence did not call for.

deleted.headline: Deleting made it worse
deleted.body: The pods were healthy. Deleting the Deployment took them away, and the Service would still have selected nothing.

saleMissed.headline: The sale started with the shop down
saleMissed.body: Ready pods with no traffic and a 503 point at the Service. Its endpoints were one command away; restarts and kubectl top were not.

stillDown.headline: Closed too soon
stillDown.body: The shop still answers 503. Check the Service's endpoints and selector, fix it, and curl before you close.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Every request gets 503 while all three pods are Running and Ready, so the app and its readiness probes are fine and the break is between the Ingress and the pods. kubectl describe svc shows Endpoints <none> and selector app=shopweb, while the pods are labeled app=shop-web: the selector matches nothing, so the EndpointSlice controller lists no pods. kubectl top shows a busy node, which is the morning report job and not the cause. The typo came from Git in the 'tidy labels' merge, and Argo CD with self-heal will keep applying it, so fix it in Git (revert and sync) rather than patching the live Service or labeling pods by hand, then confirm with a request through the Ingress.
